title: Revenue Growth is Accelerating at 3M | MMM Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc examines 3M's multi-year restructuring — divesting commodity-like businesses (revenue fell from $35B to ~$25B as a result), cutting manufacturing sites from ~110 to ~100, raising prices ~1.5% to offset oil costs, and using AI to trim overhead — and finds early signs it is working: organic revenue growth is accelerating and management guides operating margins toward 25% from ~21%. The question is whether the stock, near investor-optimism highs, is a buy. On valuation he says no: forward P/E of 16.6 sits near the high end of its recent range, and his DCF fair value is $143 vs ~$163 market, making it slightly overvalued on both lenses. He would not argue with 'fairly valued' — it is close — but wants either a pullback or more evidence the restructuring gains are durable before buying. Call: MMM AVOID at ~$163 (first tracked call on the name).

calls.thesis: 'No, not yet': slightly overvalued on DCF fair value $143 and forward P/E 16.6; wants a pullback or more restructuring evidence first. First tracked call.
calls.bull_case: Restructuring pushes operating margins toward 25%; divestitures keep working.
calls.bear_case: Tariffs/oil costs and investor optimism are already priced in.
